title: Lost Your Job? Here’s What to Do Before You Apply Anywhere
description:
Lost your job or got laid off? Your first instinct is to start applying everywhere.

Don’t.

In this video, I break down exactly what to do after losing your job — and why you should wait 5 days before applying. This simple job search strategy will help you avoid burnout, stop panic-applying, and land interviews faster.

You’ll learn:

• How to build a brag bank of measurable wins
• How to think like a hiring manager
• How to write a strong base resume (ATV method)
• How to tailor in minutes, not hours
• Why LinkedIn visibility beats cold applications

If you’re searching for:

What to do after a layoff, how to get a job fast, why you’re not getting interviews, or how to write a resume after losing your job — this is for you.

Strategy beats speed.

transcript: If I lost my job tomorrow, I'm wouldn't apply to a single job for five full days. Which sounds completely wrong because most people think moving faster gets you hired faster. It doesn't. After 20 years helping job seekers land interviews, I have learned that moving too fast waste weeks, but strategy saves time. In this video, I'm walking you through the exact five-day plan I do so you don't burn out or spin your wheels and you actually land faster. The first thing I do has nothing to do with my resume. I wouldn't even touch it yet. That surprises most people, but it matters because when you sit down stressed staring at a blank document, you don't suddenly write something brilliant. You just write more words. So instead, I start what I call brag bank. It's nothing fancy, just a simple running list of wins, projects, metrics, problems you fixed, and those moments where people relied on you or said thank you. Basically, receipts. Because if you try to remember your accomplishments later, you forget half of them almost every single time. And future you deserves better than guessing. Most people skip this next part, but it is the most important one. Stop thinking like a job seeker and start thinking like a hiring manager. I'll look at a few job descriptions I actually want. Not to apply just yet, but just to study them. And I ask myself one question. What problem are they really hiring this person to solve? Because hiring managers aren't thinking what tasks has this person done? They're thinking who can fix my mess? Are they trying to clean up chaos, improve processes, reduce turnover, or increase revenue? That's what they care about. So I match my past wins from my brag bank to those that solve the problem. That one shift alone makes your resume 10 times stronger and way easier to write. Then and only then, I build one really strong base resume. Not five versions, not rewriting everything every time I apply, and definitely not resume gymnastics. Just one clear, focused story that allows what's most important about my experience for the industry I'm targeting. Because recruiters give you about six seconds, and pretty doesn't win. Clear wins every single time. Every bullet point follows my ATV formula: action, task, value. So instead of saying managed onboarding, you say something like redesigned onboarding process cutting ramp time by 30%. Same job, way stronger proof. And just to be super clear, yes, you absolutely tailor your resume for each job, but tailoring doesn't mean starting from scratch but doing a full rewrite every time. It's small tweaks, keywords, emphasis, reordering bullets, minutes, not hours. If it's taking you two hours per application, something's not working quite right. I actually have a separate video where I walk through my five-minute tailoring method step-by-step, so you can check that out after this one. After that, I finally open LinkedIn, but still not to apply. Cold applications are honestly the slowest path. Instead, I focus on visibility first. I update my headline, turn on recruiter visibility, and reach out to warm connections and start real conversations with real humans. I look for posts from hiring managers and recruiters, not just job boards, because real conversations replace dozens of applications every single time. My video called stop applying to jobs does a deep dive on how to find these recruiters on LinkedIn. Only after all of that do I finally apply, and even then it's not 100 jobs. It's five or 10 weekly, highly targeted, tailored, intentional applications. Because 10 strong applications beat 100 weak ones all day long. Busy doesn't equal effective in the job search. Strategy does. And look, this isn't about being perfect or hyper-organized. I panic applied before, too. Most of us have. It's stressful, you feel behind, and suddenly you're rewriting your resume late at night wondering why nothing's working. I just happened to learn this the hard way that rushing creates chaos, and chaos makes the job search 10 times harder than it actually needs to be. So now, I'm slow down first, get really clear, make a simple plan, and then move. It's calmer, and honestly, it works a lot faster. If you want the exact templates and frameworks I use, the brag bank, the ATV bullets, tailoring, that's what I walk through on this channel. And in the next video, I'll show you exactly how I keep that brag bank updated so you're never starting from zero again. But for now, take a breath, don't rush, get strategic first. You've got this, and your career bestie is here to help you.
